---
title: "Explore Hospital Imaging Data"
description: "Compare CMS outpatient imaging measure distributions and state or territory summaries."
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

## Explore the reported measures

These interactive charts use the CMS reporting period **July 1, 2024–June 30, 2025**. Each record is a hospital's reported percentage for one measure. Select or hide measures in the legend, and hover over marks for details.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

imaging_url <- "https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/sites/default/files/resources/d0134a9a89e59d49426cf5a2ad063b60_1792599881/Outpatient_Imaging_Efficiency-Hospital.csv"

imaging <- read_csv(imaging_url, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(Score != "Not Available") |>
  mutate(Score = as.numeric(Score))

op10 <- imaging |>
  filter(`Measure ID` == "OP-10")

op39 <- imaging |>
  filter(`Measure ID` == "OP-39")
```

### Hospital score distributions

Each bar counts hospitals whose reported percentage falls in that score range. The measures are overlaid for comparison; use the menu to view either measure alone.

```{r}
plot_ly() |>
  add_histogram(
    data = op10,
    x = ~Score,
    name = "OP-10: Abdomen CT",
    xbins = list(size = 1.5),
    marker = list(color = "#167d8d"),
    opacity = 0.65
  ) |>
  add_histogram(
    data = op39,
    x = ~Score,
    name = "OP-39: Breast screening",
    xbins = list(size = 1.5),
    marker = list(color = "#d87850"),
    opacity = 0.65
  ) |>
  layout(
    title = "Distribution of Hospital-Reported Percentages",
    xaxis = list(title = "Reported measure percentage (%)"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Number of hospitals"),
    barmode = "overlay",
    updatemenus = list(
      list(
        type = "dropdown",
        buttons = list(
          list(
            method = "update",
            args = list(list(visible = c(TRUE, TRUE)),
                        list(title = "Both imaging measures")),
            label = "Both measures"
          ),
          list(
            method = "update",
            args = list(list(visible = c(TRUE, FALSE)),
                        list(title = "Abdomen CT (OP-10)")),
            label = "Abdomen CT (OP-10)"
          ),
          list(
            method = "update",
            args = list(list(visible = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
                        list(title = "Breast screening (OP-39)")),
            label = "Breast screening (OP-39)"
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )
```

### Compare state and territory medians

Bars show the median reported percentage among hospitals with an available score in each state or territory. A median summarizes a group; it is not a hospital rating, and differences can reflect many factors beyond care quality.

```{r}
state_summary <- imaging |>
  group_by(State, `Measure ID`, `Measure Name`) |>
  summarise(
    median_score = median(Score),
    hospitals = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(Measure = paste0(`Measure ID`, ": ", `Measure Name`))

plot_ly(
  data = state_summary,
  x = ~median_score,
  y = ~State,
  color = ~Measure,
  type = "bar",
  orientation = "h",
  text = ~paste0(
    "Hospitals with scores: ", hospitals,
    "<br>Median: ", round(median_score, 1), "%"
  ),
  hovertemplate = "%{y}<br>%{text}<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>"
) |>
  layout(
    title = "Median Reported Percentage by State or Territory",
    barmode = "group",
    xaxis = list(title = "Median reported measure percentage (%)"),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "State or territory",
      categoryorder = "array",
      categoryarray = sort(unique(state_summary$State)),
      autorange = "reversed"
    ),
    legend = list(title = list(text = "CMS measure")),
    margin = list(l = 80),
    height = 950
  )
```


## Interactive State Explorer

Choose a state or territory and an imaging measure to explore individual hospital scores. The chart updates instantly without reloading the page.

```{r}
#| results: asis

library(htmltools)

state_data <- imaging |>
  dplyr::filter(
    `Measure ID` %in% c("OP-10", "OP-39"),
    !is.na(Score),
    !is.na(State),
    !is.na(`Facility Name`)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(State, `Facility Name`)

state_choices <- sort(unique(state_data$State))

cat('<div class="explorer-controls">')
cat('<label for="state-select">State or territory</label>')
cat('<select id="state-select">')
for (s in state_choices) {
  cat(sprintf('<option value="%s">%s</option>',
              htmlEscape(s, attribute = TRUE),
              htmlEscape(s)))
}
cat('</select>')

cat('<label for="measure-select">Imaging measure</label>')
cat('<select id="measure-select">')
cat('<option value="OP-10">OP-10: Abdomen CT</option>')
cat('<option value="OP-39">OP-39: Breast screening</option>')
cat('</select>')
cat('</div>')

cat('<p id="explorer-count"></p>')
cat('<div id="hospital-explorer" style="width:100%;height:600px;"></div>')
```

```{r}
#| results: asis

library(jsonlite)

explorer_json <- state_data |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    state = State,
    measure = `Measure ID`,
    hospital = `Facility Name`,
    score = Score
  ) |>
  jsonlite::toJSON(dataframe = "rows", auto_unbox = TRUE)

cat('<script>')
cat('const hospitalData = ', explorer_json, ';', sep = '')
cat('
(function () {
  const stateSelect = document.getElementById("state-select");
  const measureSelect = document.getElementById("measure-select");
  const chart = document.getElementById("hospital-explorer");
  const count = document.getElementById("explorer-count");

  function updateExplorer() {
    const state = stateSelect.value;
    const measure = measureSelect.value;

    const selected = hospitalData
      .filter(d => d.state === state && d.measure === measure)
      .sort((a, b) => a.score - b.score);

    count.textContent =
      selected.length + " hospitals with available scores in " + state;

    const trace = {
      x: selected.map(d => d.score),
      y: selected.map(d => d.hospital),
      type: "bar",
      orientation: "h",
      marker: {
        color: measure === "OP-10" ? "#167d8d" : "#d87850"
      },
      hovertemplate: "%{y}<br>Reported score: %{x:.1f}%<extra></extra>"
    };

    const layout = {
      title: state + " — " + measure,
      xaxis: {title: "Reported percentage (%)", rangemode: "tozero"},
      yaxis: {automargin: true},
      margin: {l: 200, r: 30, t: 65, b: 65},
      height: Math.max(450, selected.length * 20 + 140)
    };

    Plotly.react(chart, [trace], layout, {responsive: true});
  }

  stateSelect.addEventListener("change", updateExplorer);
  measureSelect.addEventListener("change", updateExplorer);

  updateExplorer();
})();
')
cat('</script>')
```

The chart displays available hospital-reported percentages, not a ranking of clinical quality. Hospitals with missing scores are excluded. Differences may reflect patient populations, reporting practices, and clinical circumstances.

---

## Measure guide

- **OP-10 — Abdomen CT Use of Contrast Material:** The reported percentage of outpatient abdominal CT examinations performed both with and without contrast.
- **OP-39 — Breast Cancer Screening Recall Rates:** The reported percentage of screening mammograms followed by diagnostic imaging within 45 days.

The measures describe different processes and should not be read as a single score of hospital quality. The CMS dataset provides hospital-level reported percentages; it does not explain why a particular hospital's value differs.
